pages.text: One gray afternoon, the sky above the meadow went drip... drip... drip.
"RAIN!" cried Rabbit, and she ran so fast she tumbled into the creek — splash! "RAIN!" cried Squirrel, and he scrambled so quick he dropped every acorn he had.
"RAIN!" cried the field mice, and they dashed three different ways and bonked right into each other.
Turtle looked up at the clouds. Turtle looked at the old hollow log. And Turtle began to walk — steady, steady, steady — one foot, then the next, then the next.
Rabbit zoomed past him, soaking wet. Squirrel zipped past, empty-pawed. The mice scurried past, rubbing their noses.
When the big rain came down, everyone was tangled and dripping and grumpy — everyone but Turtle, who stepped into the hollow log, dry as toast, just as the storm began to sing on the roof.
He made room for everyone, of course. That's what Turtle does.
"How did you get here so fast?" asked Rabbit. "I didn't go fast," said Turtle. "I just kept going."
Slow and steady still gets there — calmer, and sometimes even first.
Y colorín colorado, este cuento se ha acabado.

vocab.kidDefinition: empty inside, like a log a little animal can hide in
moving the same careful way, not too fast, not stopping
ran with quick tiny steps, the way mice do
fell and rolled head over heels
